As families and friends gather across our country to celebrate Thanksgiving in this 250th anniversary year of American Independence, we pledge to carry forward the spirit of faith and fellowship that marked the first Thanksgiving feast, and we renew our mission to continue ushering in the Golden Age of America so that every citizen has the opportunity to achieve their American Dream. 

More than four centuries ago, 102 passengers set sail aboard the Mayflower on a daring voyage across the Atlantic Ocean that would forever change the course of humanity.  Fleeing religious persecution and seeking the promise of freedom found in the New World, these brave Pilgrims endured a treacherous journey and reached the shores of New England in November of 1620.  A brutal winter followed, bringing unimaginable hardship and claiming the lives of nearly half of the souls who had made the crossing.  Sustained only by their unfailing faith in Jesus Christ and the bonds they formed in caring for one another, this small community persisted with remarkable strength of spirit and laid the foundations for our civilization — forging a friendship with the Wampanoag people, learning to cultivate the land, and gathering a successful harvest in the following autumn.  Filled with gratitude to our Lord for these magnificent blessings, the Pilgrims joined the Wampanoag in a celebration that became the first Thanksgiving.

The faith and gratitude that sustained our forebears still remain at the heart of our Thanksgiving traditions and national character.  In every generation since, these enduring values have inspired proud citizens to persevere through adversity, build a land of opportunity, and pass the blessings of liberty to their children — making our Nation stronger, our future brighter, and the promise of America greater than ever before.

On this blessed day, we celebrate the glorious land that has allowed all people to worship freely and openly since its founding, and we remember that this solemn conviction anchors our national identity:  America is — and always will be — one Nation under the eternal providence and goodness of God.  Through every trial and triumph, our trust in Him has strengthened our people and inspired us to carry the flame of liberty forward.

As we gather with our loved ones to celebrate the innumerable blessings of our Republic, we also pay special tribute to the brave men and women of our Armed Forces whose commitment to duty draws them far from home and family.  Their courage and sacrifice secure the way of life we cherish, and we salute them for their unwavering dedication to defending our Nation and keeping the American People safe throughout this holiday season.

This Thanksgiving, we uphold a beloved American tradition older than our Nation itself.  May we remain steadfast in our mission to restore American greatness, faithful in our devotion to Almighty God, and united in our resolve to preserve His blessings of freedom and prosperity for centuries to come.

NOW, THEREFORE, I, DONALD J. TRUMP, President of the United States of America, by virtue of the authority vested in me by the Constitution and the laws of the United States, do hereby proclaim Thursday, November 26, 2026, as a National Day of Thanksgiving.  I encourage all Americans to gather in homes and places of worship and offer a prayer of thanks to God for our many blessings. 

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, I have hereunto set my hand this twenty-fourth day of November, in the year of our Lord two thousand twenty-six, and of the Independence of the United States of America the two hundred and fifty-first.                             

DONALD J. TRUMP

Memorandum for THE ATTORNEY GENERAL

SUBJECT:       Expeditious Enforcement of Capital Sentences and the Pursuit of Justice for Victims of Heinous Crimes

By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the laws of the United States of America, I hereby direct:

Section 1.  Background.  A prolonged delay in carrying out a death sentence is a grave offense to the justice system that denies a victim’s family the closure they deserve.  Yet capital sentences imposed upon the most vile criminals are too often frustrated by years, or even decades, of litigation.  The Department of Justice must take every step to ensure that those who commit the most heinous crimes promptly face the full consequences of their actions.

Sec. 2.  Pursuing Capital Punishment for Heinous Federal Crimes.  The Attorney General, when appropriate and consistent with applicable law, shall pursue Federal jurisdiction and seek the death penalty for particularly heinous and egregious Federal capital crimes, in addition to those identified in section 3(b) of Executive Order 14164 of January 20, 2025 (Restoring the Death Penalty and Protecting Public Safety), to include:

(a)  murder in the first degree of a minor;

(b)  murder committed in the course of rape, sexual abuse, sexual exploitation of a child, or sex trafficking; and

(c)  murder committed in the course of kidnapping or human trafficking.

Sec. 3.  Expediting the Enforcement of Capital Sentences.  The Attorney General shall take all lawful and appropriate measures to ensure that federally imposed sentences of death are carried out as expeditiously as possible.  These measures shall include:

(a)  prioritizing the prompt resolution of direct appeals, petitions for writs of habeas corpus, and other post-conviction proceedings;

(b)  opposing dilatory litigation tactics;

(c)  seeking expedited judicial consideration wherever appropriate; and

(d)  eliminating unnecessary administrative delays.

Sec. 4.  General Provisions.  (a)  Nothing in this memorandum shall be construed to impair or otherwise affect:

(i)   the authority granted by law to an executive department or agency, or the head thereof; or

(ii)  the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals.

(b)  This memorandum shall be implemented consistent with applicable law and subject to the availability of appropriations.

(c)  This memorandum is not intended to, and does not, create any right or benefit, substantive or procedural, enforceable at law or in equity by any party against the United States, its departments, agencies, or entities, its officers, employees, or agents, or any other person.

(d)  The costs for publication of this memorandum shall be borne by the Department of Justice.

                             DONALD J. TRUMP

From the moment a child is conceived, they are a gift from God, bringing hope, love, and a future filled with promise into the world.  For countless children across our Nation, adoption provides the gift of a loving family and nurturing home where they can feel safe, supported, and encouraged to pursue their own unique American Dream.  This National Adoption Month, we recognize the parents who devote their lives to protecting our Nation’s children and youth, and we rededicate ourselves to supporting those still waiting to find the loving homes they deserve.

Tragically, many children who age out of foster care face long-term socioeconomic hardships that hold them back from building a stable and prosperous future.  To combat this issue, my Administration has remained committed to aligning Federal resources to improve adoption outcomes and remove unnecessary barriers to permanency.  Last year, I proudly expanded access to the Adoption Tax Credit and made the Child Tax Credit permanent through the historic Working Families Tax Cuts Act to ease the financial challenges of adoption.  With the leadership of our great First Lady Melania Trump, I also signed the Fostering the Future for American Children and Families Executive Order, which increases educational, employment, and mentorship opportunities for youth as they transition from foster care into adulthood.

As President, I will always ensure that American children transitioning in and out of foster care have the resources they need for lifelong independence and success.  To give the next generation the head start that they deserve, the First Lady also launched Fostering the Future Accounts, America’s first savings and investment vehicle providing children in foster care with the opportunity to build long-term financial stability and expand their prospects for future success.  With this historic resource, as with Trump Accounts, America’s foster care system will harness the unparalleled generosity and resources of our Nation to serve every child.

Building on First Lady Melania Trump’s results-driven leadership, my Administration will continue to champion new policies that empower families and communities to lift up our country’s children for generations to come.  As part of this effort, we proudly launched FosteringTheFuture.gov to provide youth with accessible, reliable, and Super Intelligence-enabled support for life after foster care.  Faith-based organizations, houses of worship, businesses, nonprofits, and community groups also play a vital role in supporting adoptive parents and their children, and I encourage all Americans to put their faith and convictions into action through service, generosity, and enduring support for adoptive families.

Adoption is a beautiful reminder of what is possible when children are surrounded by love, safety, and the security to thrive.  This month, we remember those still awaiting adoption and the prospective parents preparing to welcome them, understanding that their hopes call us to purposeful action.  Strong families are sustained by strong communities, and together, we can cultivate change for others and become a source of hope and encouragement for our Nation’s children. 

NOW, THEREFORE, I, DONALD J. TRUMP, President of the United States of America, by virtue of the authority vested in me by the Constitution and the laws of the United States, do

hereby proclaim November 2026 as National Adoption Month.  I call upon all Americans to honor this month by ensuring that every child has the love and support they need to live a long, healthy, and prosperous life.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, I have hereunto set my hand this twentieth day of November, in the year of our Lord two thousand twenty-six, and of the Independence of the United States of America the two hundred and fifty-first.

                             DONALD J. TRUMP

By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the laws of the United States of America, including the Federal Property and Administrative Services Act (40 U.S.C. 101 et seq.) and the common law, it is hereby ordered:

Section 1.  Purpose and Policy.  In order to protect and serve the American people, the executive branch must be able to work closely with its employees and contractors on sensitive matters without fear that confidential information will be released to unauthorized third parties.  The doctrine of executive privilege, which the Supreme Court has recognized is inextricably rooted in the separation of powers under the Constitution, protects confidential executive branch information from disclosure.  Protecting this information from unauthorized disclosure, including to members of the Congress, is vital to the functioning of the executive branch.

The ability of the Congress to seek executive branch information is limited; it cannot seek information from executive branch departments and agencies (agencies), employees, or Federal contractors without a valid legislative purpose that does not intrude on core Executive functions.  Nor can the Congress obtain privileged information, including information shared between Federal employees and Federal contractors, before the executive branch has an opportunity to assert relevant privileges.  Despite these bedrock protections, certain congressional leaders have threatened to intrude on these Executive prerogatives by seeking confidential executive branch information from agencies and harassing private companies that contract with the Federal Government.  The executive branch has a compelling interest in its confidential information, and the right to protect that information from disclosure even by Federal contractors pursuant to a congressional request. 

A lack of coordination between Federal contractors and the executive branch undermines the ability of contractors to provide economical and efficient goods and services.  If Federal contractors fail to provide timely notice and coordinate with the White House and agencies prior to responding to congressional requests for information, the executive branch may be required to intervene or engage in separate litigation to defend its rights.  Federal contractors also may be unaware of the executive branch’s interests and positions, resulting in duplicative and wasteful efforts.  Federal contractors and the executive branch engaging in separate strategies and litigation regarding the same requests and information is inefficient and wastes taxpayer resources.  Moreover, the executive branch engages in sensitive and vital work with contractors, including on matters of national and homeland security.  Such work often involves confidential information.  If the executive branch cannot be assured that those communications will remain confidential, agencies and the White House will be chilled from sharing sensitive information with contractors, which will stymie the operation of critical Government programs.  An inability to safely and freely share such information with Federal contractors will also substantially reduce the efficiency of those contractors and the work being provided to the public.  The executive branch will thus have to find alternative means of carrying out similar functions, reducing and even eliminating reliance on Federal contractors for certain purposes.  Such an outcome is neither efficient nor desirable for the Federal Government or its contractors.

It is therefore the policy of the United States to protect confidential information and enhance economy and efficiency in Federal contracting by preventing and prohibiting uncoordinated disclosures of information pursuant to congressional requests.

Sec. 2.  Requirements for Federal Contractors.  In order to protect the executive branch’s interests and rights, and to ensure economical and efficient work with Federal contractors, all Federal contractors must immediately:

(a)  notify the White House and the contracting agencies of any pending or future congressional request respecting the contractors’ communications or work with the executive branch; and abide by any instructions received from the White House and contracting agency related to the withholding of communications that the White House or the agency has determined are protected by executive privilege.

(b)  Agencies shall coordinate with the White House and contractors on appropriate responses to such congressional requests, including the application or assertion of any relevant privileges.

(c)  This section also applies to subcontractors working for a Federal contractor on a Federal contract.  Agencies shall take steps to require Federal contractors to be responsible for ensuring that subcontractors working on Federal contracts comply with this section.

Sec. 3.  Implementation.  (a)  Each agency shall promptly inform all contractors and subcontractors of the obligations in this order and shall require such contractors and subcontractors to comply with the requirements set forth in section 2 of this order.

(b)  The Office of Management and Budget shall develop guidance on how agencies can ensure that contractors are complying with the requirements set forth in section 2 of this order and steps that agencies should take to ensure adequate coordination between the contracting agencies, contractors, and White House to enhance efficiency and the protection of Executive information.

Sec. 4.  Enforcement.  If a Federal contractor or subcontractor fails to comply with the requirements set forth in section 2 of this order, contracting agencies shall consider whether to take all appropriate actions, consistent with applicable law, to enforce the terms of this order, including the potential termination or cancellation of contracts and the potential debarment or suspension of contractors.

Sec. 5.  Severability.  If any provision of this order, or the application of any provision to any person or circumstance, is held to be invalid, the remainder of this order and the application of its provisions to any other persons or circumstances shall not be affected thereby.

Sec. 6.  General Provisions.  (a)  Nothing in this order shall be construed to impair or otherwise affect:

(i)   the authority granted by law to an executive department or agency, or the head thereof; or

(ii)  the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals.

(b)  This order shall be implemented consistent with applicable law and subject to the availability of appropriations.

(c)  This order is not intended to, and does not, create any right or benefit, substantive or procedural, enforceable at law or in equity by any party against the United States, its departments, agencies, or entities, its officers, employees, or agents, or any other person.

(d)  The costs for publication of this order shall be borne by the Department of Labor.

                             DONALD J. TRUMP

BY THE PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA

A PROCLAMATION

For over 250 years, the liberties and freedoms of every American have been safeguarded by the heroic men and women who have faithfully served in the United States Armed Forces.  This Veterans Day, we honor our Nation’s cherished veterans and recommit to strengthen the support and resources they have so rightly earned.

From the battle for our independence during the Revolutionary War and the fight for the future of humanity in World War II to the ongoing battles to defend America’s security and protect her people, the countless veterans who have taken up arms have ensured that generations of Americans could enjoy the many blessings of our great Nation.  These selfless men and women have committed their lives to defending our families, our freedom, and our great American values.  We will never forget the price they have paid for our homeland.

As they sacrificed for our freedom, so too must our Nation ensure their welfare.  At my direction, the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is restructuring to put veterans at the forefront of every decision.  The VA processed a record 3.1 million disability claims this year.  In my second term, we have also slashed the VA’s claims backlog by more than 70 percent and opened 47 new health care facilities, expanding access to world-class care for veterans in communities across our country.

Every American owes our veterans an eternal debt of gratitude, and no one who has worn our Nation’s uniform should ever be homeless.  That is why I will never stop fighting until every veteran has the housing and mental health support and treatment they need.  Additionally, I established the National Center for Warrior Independence last year with a goal of housing up to 6,000 homeless veterans by 2028.  Last year alone, we housed nearly 52,000 homeless veterans, the most in 7 years, and under my leadership, every veteran who served our Nation in the Armed Forces will have a place to call home.

My Administration is working tirelessly to provide our veterans with the resources and support they so dearly deserve.  As President, I have eliminated burdensome and needless red tape and ensured that every veteran receives the exceptional care they are entitled to.  With an Executive Order I signed in September, we are also accelerating veterans’ access to benefits and employment opportunities through modernized data management and sharing between the VA and the Department of War.  So long as I am President, we will continue to relentlessly expand veterans’ access to health care, education, and job opportunities and aggressively deliver this life-changing support.

Millions of brave men and women have served in the United States Armed Forces with heroic determination and sacrifice, safeguarding our security, prosperity, and sovereignty.  Today, we are united in gratitude for the courage of our Airmen, Coast Guardsmen, Marines, Sailors, Soldiers, and Guardians, and we thank the families who have stood with them in their service to our country.  Through the unmatched prowess and strength of America’s veterans, the freedoms we cherish, our glorious American way of life, and the greatest country the world has ever known will endure for centuries to come.  We will always uphold the legacy of our veterans and ensure our Nation remains safe, strong, and secure in the blessings of liberty.

In respectful recognition of the contributions our service members have made to advance peace and freedom around the world, the Congress has provided (5 U.S.C. 6103(a)) that November 11 of each year shall be set aside as a legal public holiday to honor our Nation’s veterans.

NOW, THEREFORE, I, DONALD J. TRUMP, President of the United States of America, do hereby proclaim November 11, 2026, as Veterans Day.  I encourage all Americans to reflect on the fearlessness and sacrifice of our veterans through public ceremonies and private thoughts and prayers of gratitude.  I call upon Federal, State, and local officials to display the flag of the United States and to participate in patriotic activities in their communities.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, I have hereunto set my hand this tenth day of November, in the year of our Lord two thousand twenty-six, and of the Independence of the United States of America the two hundred and fifty-first.

                             DONALD J. TRUMP

MEMORANDUM FOR THE SECRETARY OF THE INTERIOR, THE SECRETARY OF AGRICULTURE, THE ADMINISTRATOR OF THE ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AGENCY

SUBJECT:       Presidential Determination Concerning Wildfire Suppression Activities in the United States

By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the laws of the United States of America, including section 313 of the Federal Water Pollution Control Act, as amended (33 U.S.C. 1323), I determine that it is in the paramount interest of the United States to exempt firefighting activities, including the aerial use, deployment, and discharge of fire retardants, conducted by the United States Forest Service, the Department of the Interior, and any other executive departments and agencies (agencies) and their contractors (aspects of which are the subject of litigation in Forest Service Employees for Environmental Ethics v. U.S. Forest Service, No. CV-22-168-M-DLC (D. Mont.)) from Federal, State, interstate, and local requirements, administrative authority, and process and sanctions respecting the control and abatement of water pollution.  

Therefore, pursuant to subsection (a) of section 313 of the Federal Water Pollution Control Act, as amended (33 U.S.C.  1323(a)), I hereby exempt firefighting activities conducted by the United States Forest Service, the Department of the Interior, and any other agencies and their contractors, including the aerial use, deployment, and discharge of fire retardants, from Federal, State, interstate, and local requirements, administrative authority, and process and sanctions respecting the control and abatement of water pollution; except that no exemption is hereby granted from the requirements of 33 U.S.C. 1316 and 1317.

The exemption granted by this memorandum shall be for the 1-year period beginning November 10, 2026, and ending November 10, 2027.

Nothing herein is intended to:  (a) imply that in the absence of such a Presidential exemption, the Clean Water Act or any other provision of law would require the United States Forest Service or other agencies to obtain permits pertaining to the control and abatement of water pollution for the exempted operations; or (b) limit the applicability or enforcement of any other requirement of law applicable to the United States Forest Service, the Department of the Interior, or any other agencies and their contractors regarding such agencies’ firefighting activities.

The Secretary of Agriculture is authorized and directed to publish this determination in the Federal Register.

BY THE PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA

A PROCLAMATION

The Oval Office stands as one of the most recognizable and historically significant spaces in the United States.  Since its establishment in its present location and form during the administration of President Franklin D. Roosevelt, it has served as the principal working office of the President of the United States.  Decisions of profound national and international consequence have been made within its walls.  It has hosted heads of state, shaped the daily conduct of the executive branch, and become a symbol of the American Presidency itself.

The room’s distinctive oval design, first introduced in the West Wing under President William Howard Taft and refined in the early 1930s, reflects both practical and ceremonial purposes.  Its architecture, finishes of lasting character, and continuous association with the Presidency give the Oval Office exceptional and unique value in illustrating the history of the United States.  The Oval Office possesses an unmatched and unique combination of location, design, setting, materials, workmanship, and an association with historical events that are embedded in our national consciousness. 

The White House and its grounds are Federal property administered as part of the President’s Park by the National Park Service and are already recognized as a National Historic Landmark.  Nonetheless, the Oval Office merits specific recognition and protective management as a discrete historic structure of national significance.

WHEREAS, section 320301 of title 54, United States Code (the “Antiquities Act”), authorizes the President, in the President’s discretion, to declare by public proclamation historic landmarks, historic and prehistoric structures, and other objects of historic or scientific interest that are situated upon the lands owned or controlled by the Federal Government to be national monuments, and to reserve as a part thereof parcels of land, the limits of which shall be confined to the smallest area compatible with the proper care and management of the objects to be protected;

WHEREAS, it is in the public interest to preserve the Oval Office as a national monument; and

WHEREAS, I find that the boundaries of the Oval Office represent the smallest area compatible with the proper care and management of the objects of historic and scientific interest identified above;

NOW, THEREFORE, I, DONALD J. TRUMP, President of the United States of America, by the authority vested in me by section 320301 of title 54, United States Code, hereby proclaim the Oval Office as the Oval Office National Monument (monument).

The monument shall consist of the Oval Office itself (Room 110) together with the Outer Oval Office (Rooms 106 and 108) and the Cabinet Room (Room 105).  The boundaries of the monument are the smallest area compatible with the proper care and management of the objects of historic interest to be protected.

The Secretary of the Interior (Secretary), through the National Park Service, shall manage the monument in a manner that protects its historic character, architectural integrity, and association with the Presidency.  The Secretary shall:

(1)  develop and implement a management plan, in consultation with the White House Office of Administration and other relevant executive departments, agencies, and offices, that prioritizes the preservation of the monument’s structural and significant architectural features;

(2)  require documentation, review, and consideration of alternatives before any action that would substantially alter or demolish the monument or its essential architectural elements;

(3)  ensure that any proposed changes affecting the monument’s historic character are evaluated for consistency with its national significance; and

(4)  coordinate with the Committee for the Preservation of the White House and other appropriate advisory bodies.

The Secretary is directed to take all necessary steps to implement this proclamation.

Nothing in this proclamation shall be construed to restrict the President’s authority to redecorate the monument, select furnishings, or make ordinary operational and security modifications that do not substantially impair the monument’s historic structure or architectural character.

Nothing in this proclamation alters existing statutory exemptions applicable to the White House under the National Historic Preservation Act or diminishes the Congress’s authority over Federal property.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, I have hereunto set my hand this fifth day of November, in the year of our Lord two thousand twenty-six, and of the Independence of the United States of America the two hundred and fifty-first.

                             DONALD J. TRUMP

BY THE PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA

A PROCLAMATION

For more than a century, human freedom has been threatened by communist and socialist ideologies that eliminate individual opportunity, subjugate individuals to the state, and extinguish the God-given rights upon which free nations are built.  This Anti-Communism Week, we are reminded of the devastating consequences of state control over human thought, creativity, and political expression, resulting in suffering, poverty, exploitation, violence, and misery for millions, and we renew our commitment to protect the sacred values of life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness from the chains of tyranny.

Our Republic was founded upon the enduring conviction that our rights are inherent, our liberties are sacred, and our Government derives its just powers from the consent of the governed.  These principles have defined our national character for over 250 years and continue to distinguish our way of life from that of all other countries on Earth.

Today, however, our American experiment faces renewed threats as socialist, communist, and radical leftist ideologies find increased expression in our Nation.  We must remain vigilant in defending the principles that sustain our Republic and ensure the lessons of history are never forgotten nor repeated.  Under my leadership, America will never fall victim to these evil ideologies, and the United States will never become a communist country.

The story of America is, above all, a story of a Nation uniting as one, standing up to tyranny, and charting its own destiny as a free and self-governing Republic.  As President, I will always protect the founding principles for which so many fought and died.  Together, we will defend our Constitution, which protects our freedoms; uphold the dignity of every individual; strengthen the free market, which has made us the most prosperous country ever to exist; and ensure that the promise of America remains alive and well for generations to come.

This week, we honor the victims of socialism and communism by remembering their lives, defending the freedoms that were denied, renewing our resolve to safeguard the Republic entrusted to us, and reminding ourselves that what we have created as a Nation stands as the greatest testament to human freedom in the history of the world.

NOW, THEREFORE, I, DONALD J. TRUMP, President of the United States of America, by virtue of the authority vested in me by the Constitution and the laws of the United States, do hereby proclaim the week of November 1 through November 7 as Anti-Communism Week.  I call upon all Americans to stand firm in their defense against any threat to the American way of life and to protect our burning flame of liberty from the darkness of communism. 

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, I have hereunto set my hand this third day of November, in the year of our Lord two thousand twenty-six, and of the Independence of the United States of America the two hundred and fifty-first.

                             DONALD J. TRUMP

BY THE PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA

A PROCLAMATION

It is America’s destiny to explore and expand our frontiers beyond Earth to the farthest depths of space.  Today, my Administration reaffirms that our solar system and all of outer space beyond Earth are the province of all humans, and that our Nation will lead the way in the exploration, development, use, and settlement of these new frontiers — forging an interplanetary civilization founded on the enduring and inalienable rights of freedom and individual liberty.  

From the intrepid Apollo 11 astronauts who took humanity’s first steps on the Moon to the pioneering rovers that explored the surface of Mars, the United States has always blazed a trail into the great unknown, shattering boundaries and pushing mankind to extraordinary new heights.  Behind each triumph are generations of astronauts, scientists, engineers, and workers whose tireless dedication and unmatched ingenuity turn impossible dreams into reality. 

Under my leadership, the United States is once again writing a bold new chapter in space exploration.  This past April, the Artemis II mission successfully carried astronauts around the Moon and farther from Earth than any human had ever traveled before.  This historic voyage is only the beginning.  Next summer, Artemis III will undertake one of the most complex and consequential test flight campaigns in the history of our Nation’s space program.

This proud legacy of innovation is our sacred inheritance, and our Nation bears the solemn responsibility to advance it by continuing to open new horizons of exploration and discovery.  Through the landmark Executive Orders and directives I have signed, we are reinvigorating human spaceflight, unleashing a competitive and thriving commercial space industry, and ensuring American space superiority for all eternity.  We will return to the Moon by 2028, lay the foundation for a permanent American lunar presence, and hasten the day when an American becomes the first human to set foot on the red dunes of Mars.  Together, we will build the facilities, develop the resources, and establish a permanent presence in space to extend the reach of American exploration, preserve our frontier spirit, and strengthen our national security for centuries to come.  The nation that leads in space will shape the future of humanity — and that nation will be the United States of America. 

Today, we renew our solemn and righteous mission to propel humanity toward the farthest reaches of the universe.  We reaffirm that the United States will lead the way in this bold endeavor, for the nation with the best scientific understanding of space, the most advanced space economy, and the greatest spacefaring citizens, will be the most prosperous nation for centuries to come.  Above all, we pledge to carry our sacred values of faith and freedom wherever we journey, so that freedom may forever ring among the stars and beyond.

NOW, THEREFORE, I, DONALD J. TRUMP, President of the United States of America, by virtue of the authority vested in me by the Constitution and the laws of the United States, do hereby proclaim that the solar system and all of outer space beyond Earth are the province of all humans and are open to exploration, development, use, and the establishment of a permanent presence by American citizens consistent with United States law and the international obligations of the United States.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, I have hereunto set my hand this third day of November, in the year of our Lord two thousand twenty-six, and of the Independence of the United States of America the two hundred and fifty-first.

                             DONALD J. TRUMP

BY THE PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA

A PROCLAMATION

1.  Within the past 90 days, the Secretary of Commerce (Secretary) transmitted to me a report on his investigation into the effects of imports of robotics and industrial machinery, as well as their parts and components (together, components), on the national security of the United States under section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962, as amended, 19 U.S.C. 1862 (section 232).  Based on the facts considered in that investigation, and taking into account the close relation of the economic welfare of the Nation to our national security and other relevant factors, see section 232(d) (19 U.S.C. 1862(d)), the Secretary found and advised me of his opinion that robotics, industrial machinery, and their components are being imported into the United States in such quantities and under such circumstances as to threaten to impair the national security of the United States.

2.  Nearly all modern defense systems and critical infrastructure sectors require the use of robotics or industrial machinery to function or be manufactured effectively and efficiently.  Robotics and industrial machinery are critical to virtually all modern manufacturing processes, including for defense, commercial, and dual-use purposes.  Robotics and industrial machinery enable defense readiness and design, production, and sustainment activities across a wide range of defense applications.  Furthermore, robotics and industrial machinery generate substantial economic value and support important economic activities, including approximately $7.1 trillion in shipments of manufactured goods in 2024 and the production of approximately $86 billion worth of equipment in 2024.  

3.  The Secretary found that robotics and industrial machinery support the production of essential, state-of-the-art defense systems, such as aircraft, tanks, ships, weapons, and munitions, as well as certain military and law enforcement activities.  For example, advanced robots — such as autonomous robots, humanoid and quadruped robots, and autonomous ground vehicles — provide combat support to the United States military, including by conducting intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance missions and by handling dangerous tasks, such as casualty extraction and mine detection and clearing.  Robotics and industrial machinery also enable the defense industry to automate the building of essential defense products, such as missiles, aircraft, and ships, allowing production activities to last longer and for repetitive tasks to be performed with minimal error.  Indeed, the defense industrial base’s ability to surge production, including during wartime or armed conflict, relies on industrial robotics and machinery.

4.  The Secretary found that robotics and industrial machines are also crucial to the United States’ critical infrastructure sectors and other key aspects of the United States economy.  Industrial robots and machines are used to create products and parts that are used across all 16 critical infrastructure sectors of the United States.  For example, industrial robots are heavily used in the automotive, electrical, and electronics industries and are also meaningfully used in the metal and machinery, plastic and chemical products, and food and beverage industries.  Similarly, industrial machinery carries out critical functions across various industries and in the manufacturing process for a range of goods, including construction equipment, electronics, medical devices, metal fabrication, motor vehicles, and aircraft.  And because industrial robots and machinery serve end-use industries and contribute to equipment manufacturing and product creation efforts, they carry expansive downstream implications for the United States economy.  Thus, robotics and industrial machines are a driving force behind critical infrastructure sectors and are crucial to the national and economic security interests of the United States.

5.  The Secretary found that the United States relies on foreign imports for most types of robotics and industrial machinery and for their components.  The value of robotics, industrial machinery, and their components imported into the United States has increased over the last decade and is projected to continue to increase.  This import reliance poses risks to the United States industrial base and threatens the long-term competitiveness of the United States in a sector that is increasingly vital to national security.

6.  The Secretary also found that robotics, industrial machinery, and their components from certain foreign entities pose unique security and safety risks.  Robotics and industrial machinery are integrated into many manufacturing and defense systems and routinely process and store sensitive data.  These technologies, when sourced from foreign entities, can pose significant cybersecurity vulnerabilities that can result in severe consequences to the United States. 

7.  The Secretary found that the domestic industry does not produce enough robotics, industrial machinery, and their components to meet national security needs, and that the need for domestically produced robotics, industrial machinery, and their components will only increase.  Despite a recent surge in investments in manufacturing facilities in the United States, the United States still produces less robotics and industrial equipment than it consumes, lacks the capacity to satisfy the need for robotics and industrial machinery with domestic sources, and underutilizes its manufacturing capacity for robotics, industrial equipment, and their components.  According to the Secretary, without intervention, challenges for United States manufacturers investing in robotics and industrial machinery will likely continue.  In the Secretary’s opinion, it is vital to take action to strengthen, expand, and modernize the domestic manufacturing and industrial base for robotics, industrial machinery, and their components.

8.  In light of these findings and other findings in the Secretary’s report, the Secretary recommended various actions to adjust the imports of robotics, industrial machinery, and their components so that such imports will not threaten to impair the national security.

9.  After considering the Secretary’s report, the factors in section 232(d) (19 U.S.C. 1862(d)), and other relevant factors and information, I concur with the Secretary’s finding that robotics, industrial machinery, and their components are being imported into the United States in such quantities and under such circumstances as to threaten to impair the national security of the United States.  In my judgment, and in light of the Secretary’s report, the factors in section 232(d) (19 U.S.C. 1862(d)), and other relevant factors and information, I determine that it is necessary and appropriate to enter into negotiations with trading partners to adjust imports of robotics, industrial machinery, and their components so that such imports will not threaten to impair the national security of the United States.

10.  I therefore direct the Secretary and the United States Trade Representative (Trade Representative) to jointly pursue negotiations of agreements or continue any current negotiations of agreements to address the threatened impairment of the national security with respect to imported robotics, industrial machinery, and their components, with any foreign trading partner the Secretary and the Trade Representative deem appropriate, and to update me on the progress of such negotiations within 180 days of the date of this proclamation.  Under current circumstances and in light of future requirements of the United States, this course of action is necessary and appropriate to address the threatened impairment of the national security. 

11.  Section 232 authorizes the President to take action to adjust the imports of an article and its derivatives that are being imported into the United States in such quantities or under such circumstances as to threaten to impair the national security.  Section 232 includes the authority to adopt and carry out a plan of action, with adjustments over time, to address the national security threat.  That initial plan of action may include negotiations of agreements along with other actions to adjust imports to address the national security threat, including tariffs, duties, quotas, and fees.  If action under section 232 includes the negotiation of an agreement, such as one contemplated in section 232(c)(3)(A)(i) (19 U.S.C. 1862(c)(3)(A)(i)), the President may also take other actions he deems necessary to adjust imports to eliminate the threat that the imported article poses to the national security, including if such an agreement is not entered into within 180 days of the date of this proclamation, is not being carried out, or is ineffective.  See 19 U.S.C. 1862(c)(3)(A).

12.  Section 604 of the Trade Act of 1974, as amended (19 U.S.C. 2483) (section 604), authorizes the President to embody in the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States the substance of statutes affecting import treatment, and actions thereunder, including the removal, modification, continuance, or imposition of any rate of duty or other import restriction.

NOW, THEREFORE, I, DONALD J. TRUMP, President of the United States of America, by the authority vested in me by the Constitution and the laws of the United States, including section 232; section 604; and section 301 of title 3, United States Code, do hereby proclaim as follows:

(1)  The Secretary and the Trade Representative shall jointly pursue or continue pursuing negotiations of agreements to address the threatened impairment of the national security with respect to imports of robotics, industrial machinery, and their components.  Depending on the status or outcome of such negotiations, I may consider alternative remedies in the future, including imposing or modifying tariffs, duties, quotas, and fees; and establishing a program to incentivize new investment in United States production of robotics and industrial machinery, as well as their parts and components.

     (2)  The Secretary and the Trade Representative, in consultation with any other senior executive branch official they deem appropriate, shall, from time to time, update me on the status or outcome of the negotiations described in this proclamation.  The Secretary and the Trade Representative shall provide one of these updates within 180 days of the date of this proclamation.

(3)  The Secretary shall continue to monitor imports of robotics, industrial machinery, and their components and shall, from time to time, in consultation with any senior executive branch officials the Secretary deems appropriate, review the status of such imports with respect to the national security.  The Secretary shall inform me of any circumstances that, in the Secretary’s opinion, might indicate the need for further action by the President under section 232.

(4)  Any provision of previous proclamations and Executive Orders that is inconsistent with this proclamation is superseded to the extent of such inconsistency.  If any provision of this proclamation or the application of any provision of this proclamation to any individual or circumstance is held to be invalid, the remainder of this proclamation and the application of its provisions to any other individual or circumstance shall not be affected.

     IN WITNESS WHEREOF, I have hereunto set my hand this

twenty-eighth day of October, in the year of our Lord two thousand twenty-six, and of the Independence of the United States of America the two hundred and fifty-first.

                             DONALD J. TRUMP

BY THE PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA

A PROCLAMATION

1.  In Proclamation 11048 of July 20, 2026 (Imposing Additional Duties To Offset Canadian Discrimination Against the Commerce of the United States With Respect to Motor Vehicles), I found as a fact that Canada is discriminating in fact against the commerce of the United States through Canada’s motor vehicle tariff scheme; that this discrimination places the commerce of the United States at a disadvantage compared to the commerce of other countries; and that Canada’s imposition is unreasonable, is not equally enforced upon the like articles of every foreign country, and places a burden on the commerce of the United States.  To offset the burden or disadvantage on U.S. commerce from Canada’s discrimination or unreasonable and unequal imposition on U.S. auto and auto parts exports, I imposed under section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930 (19 U.S.C. 1338) (section 338) additional ad valorem duties, effective August 19, 2026, on certain products of Canada.

2.  In Proclamation 11056 of August 18, 2026 (Temporary Suspension of Additional Duties To Offset Canadian Discrimination Against the Commerce of the United States With Respect to Alcoholic Beverages, Dairy, and Motor Vehicles), I temporarily suspended for 3 days the effective date of the additional ad valorem duties imposed under Proclamation 11048 after Canada expressed a commitment to remove the discrimination or unreasonable and unequal imposition at issue in Proclamation 11048.

3.  On August 21, 2026, Canada reneged on its commitment, ceased negotiating in good faith, and did not remove the discrimination or unreasonable and unequal imposition at issue in Proclamation 11048. 

4.  Accordingly, at 12:01 a.m. eastern time on August 22, 2026, the 3-day suspension imposed by Proclamation 11056 lapsed, and the additional ad valorem duties imposed under Proclamation 11048 became effective.

5. In Proclamation 11065 of September 8, 2026 (Modifying the Scope of Products of Canada Subject to the Additional Duties Imposed To Offset Canadian Discrimination Against the Commerce of the United States With Respect to Motor Vehicles), I modified the duties imposed under Proclamation 11048 after receiving certain information, opinions, and recommendations from senior executive branch officials to continue offsetting the burden or disadvantage on U.S. commerce and better serve the public interest.

6.  I have received certain additional information, opinions, and recommendations from senior executive branch officials on the status of the circumstances involved in Proclamation 11048 and the effect of the additional ad valorem duties imposed in Proclamation 11048, as amended, including how effectively those duties are offsetting the burden or disadvantage on U.S. commerce.  According to senior executive branch officials, although the additional ad valorem duties imposed in Proclamation 11048, as amended, offset the burden or disadvantage on U.S. commerce, modifying the scope of products subject to the additional ad valorem duties imposed in Proclamation 11048, as amended, would still offset the burden or disadvantage on U.S. commerce and better serve the public interest.  In my senior executive branch officials’ opinion, modifying the scope of products subject to the additional ad valorem duties imposed in Proclamation 11048, as amended, is required by the public interests and is consistent with the interests of the United States.

7.  After considering the information, opinions, and recommendations that have been provided to me by senior executive branch officials, among other relevant information and considerations, I determine that the public interests require modifying the scope of products subject to the additional ad valorem duties imposed in Proclamation 11048, as amended. 

8.  In my judgment, the modification in this proclamation will offset the burden or disadvantage on U.S. commerce, is consistent with the public interests and the interests of the United States, is required by the public interests, and will better serve the public interest.

9.  Section 338 authorizes the President, if he determines it will serve the public interest, to offset any burden or disadvantage placed on the commerce of the United States by an unequal imposition or discrimination by a foreign country by specifying and declaring additional duties not to exceed 50 percent ad valorem (or its equivalent) and not to take effect earlier than 30 days after the President’s proclamation finding that a foreign country is imposing an unreasonable charge, exaction, regulation, or limitation that is not equally enforced on the like articles of every foreign country, or discriminates in fact against U.S. commerce in a way that places the commerce of the United States at a disadvantage compared to the commerce of any foreign country.  Section 338 also authorizes the President to suspend, revoke, supplement, or amend any proclamation under section 338 whenever the President deems that the public interests require such action.  Further, section 338 authorizes the President to exclude from importation articles of the foreign country if the foreign country maintains or increases the discrimination against the commerce of the United States and the President deems the exclusion to be consistent with the public interests and the interests of the United States.

10.  Section 604 of the Trade Act of 1974, as amended (19 U.S.C. 2483) (section 604), authorizes the President to embody in the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States (HTSUS) the substance of statutes affecting import treatment, and actions thereunder, including the removal, modification, continuance, or imposition of any rate of duty or other import restriction.

NOW, THEREFORE, I, DONALD J. TRUMP, President of the United States of America, by the authority vested in me by the Constitution and the laws of the United States, including section 338; section 301 of title 3, United States Code; and section 604, do hereby proclaim as follows:

(1)  Except as otherwise provided in this proclamation, certain products of Canada, as set forth in Annex I, Part A to this proclamation, imported into the United States shall no longer be subject to the additional ad valorem duty of 50 percent imposed pursuant to Proclamation 11048, as amended.  In addition, certain products of Canada, as set forth in Annex I, Part B to this proclamation, imported into the United States shall be subject to the additional ad valorem duty of 50 percent imposed pursuant to Proclamation 11048, as amended.  The duties imposed pursuant to Proclamation 11048, as amended, and as modified in this proclamation, shall apply in addition to duties imposed pursuant to section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962, as amended (19 U.S.C. 1862).  These changes shall be effective with respect to goods entered for consumption, or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption, on or after 12:01 a.m. eastern time on October 30, 2026.

(2)  The HTSUS is modified as provided in Annex II to this proclamation, effective with respect to goods entered for consumption, or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption, on or after 12:01 a.m. eastern time on October 30, 2026, and the modifications shall continue in effect unless this action is expressly suspended, revoked, supplemented, amended, or terminated.

(3)  The head of each executive department and agency (agency) is authorized to and shall take all appropriate measures within the agency’s authority to implement this proclamation.  The head of each agency may, consistent with applicable law, including section 301 of title 3, United States Code, redelegate the authority to take such appropriate measures within the agency.

(4)  The Commissioner of U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), in consultation with the Secretary of the Treasury, the Secretary of Commerce, and the United States Trade Representative, is authorized to issue such rules, regulations, guidance, instructions, or determinations as may be necessary to implement this proclamation and is authorized to take any necessary measures to administer this proclamation.

(5)  The Commissioner of CBP, in consultation with the Secretary of the Treasury, the Secretary of Commerce, the United States Trade Representative, the Chairman of the United States International Trade Commission, and any other senior executive branch official the Commissioner of CBP deems appropriate, shall determine whether any additional modifications to the HTSUS are necessary to effectuate this proclamation and shall make such modifications to the HTSUS through notice in the Federal Register, including any technical or ministerial correction to the annexes to this proclamation.

(6)  For any rule or regulation the Commissioner of CBP makes to implement this proclamation, the Commissioner of CBP shall, to the extent required by law, obtain the approval of the President or the United States Trade Representative.  The United States Trade Representative is delegated the President’s approval authority in 19 U.S.C. 1338(h).

(7)  Any provision of previous proclamations and Executive Orders that is inconsistent with this proclamation is superseded to the extent of such inconsistency.  

(8)  If any provision of this proclamation or the application of any provision to any individual or circumstance is held to be invalid, the remainder of this proclamation and the application of its provisions to any other individuals or circumstances shall not be affected.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, I have hereunto set my hand this twenty-third day of October, in the year of our Lord two thousand twenty-six, and of the Independence of the United States of America the two hundred and fifty-first.

Annex I

Annex II

                             DONALD J. TRUMP

By the President of the United States of America

A Proclamation

Across our Nation’s harbors and fishing communities, the unrivaled skill and resolve of American fishermen and seafood producers turn the bounty of our waters into food for our families and enduring economic strength.  Food security is national security — we recognize that our fisheries are a vital pillar of American independence.  This National Seafood Month, I join the American people in celebrating these hardworking men and women and reaffirm my commitment to helping them compete, prosper, and lead the world in seafood production.

From the fishing ports of early America to today’s seafood farms and processing plants, this great industry has rewarded enterprise, sustained family businesses, and helped forge the unmatched spirit of determination that defines our maritime workforce.  For generations, our fishermen have braved rough seas and punishing storms, spending long days far from home to earn an honest living and provide for the people they love.  Across our land, the incredible American seafood industry harvests nearly 8.5 billion pounds of world-class food annually, sustains more than a million jobs, and fuels more than $173 billion in commerce, bringing wealth and opportunity to communities across our great Nation.  And now, as we usher in a new Golden Age of seafood production, we are ensuring our fishing communities remain places where the next generation can raise a family, build a business, and pursue their own share of the American Dream.

Since returning to office, I have taken decisive action to restore American seafood competitiveness and give our fishing communities greater freedom to grow and succeed.  Last year, I signed an Executive Order to restore American seafood competitiveness, and my Administration recently launched the Department of Agriculture Office of Seafood.  I have also signed three proclamations to restore commercial fishing access to nearly 5,000 square miles in the Atlantic Ocean and to hundreds of thousands of square miles in the Pacific, enabling American vessels to work additional fishing grounds and compete more effectively in the global seafood market.  Under my leadership, we delivered the largest single-year quota increase in the history of the United States Atlantic bluefin tuna fishery, secured a massive 1,200 percent quota increase for Atlantic mackerel, and revived the West Coast salmon season to yield the first full commercial fishery in 3 years.  My Administration was also proud to allocate $123.6 million in fishery disaster assistance to help communities recover from devastating losses, strengthen shoreside infrastructure, and support job retraining to help workers get back on their feet.  We will continue slashing burdensome regulations so our fishermen can reinvest in their fleets, expand their operations, and keep more of what they earn.  Through these historic efforts, we are putting American fishermen first and fighting to make our Nation the strongest, most successful seafood producer in the world.

As our Nation celebrates National Seafood Month, we give thanks to the families whose skill and sacrifice have built and sustained this essential American industry for over 250 years.  We will stand with them as we build a future of thriving ports, successful businesses, and an American seafood industry that is stronger, more competitive, and more prosperous than ever before.

NOW, THEREFORE, I, DONALD J. TRUMP, President of the United States of America, by virtue of the authority vested in me by the Constitution and the laws of the United States, do hereby proclaim October 2026 as National Seafood Month.  I call upon all Americans to express their thanks for the American citizens who sustain this crucial industry, and to mark this month with appropriate events and ceremonies.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, I have hereunto set my hand this twenty-second day of October, in the year of our Lord two thousand twenty-six, and of the Independence of the United States of America the two hundred and fifty-first.

                             DONALD J. TRUMP

By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the laws of the United States of America, it is hereby ordered:

Section 1.  Purpose.  The American Dream of homeownership is a vital pillar of our great country.  It is the policy of my Administration to reduce regulatory barriers to mortgage origination and costs impeding homeownership; embrace innovative risk and value assessment technologies that incorporate Super Intelligence to drive down mortgage and homeownership costs; and promote competition and innovation throughout the housing and mortgage market.

Sec. 2.  Proactive Cancellation of Excessive Mortgage Insurance.  (a)  The Director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency (Director) shall, if he determines that it is in the best interests of the Federal National Mortgage Association and the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation (Enterprises) or the Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA), and the American public, direct the Enterprises to establish a pilot program, applicable only to mortgages made after the establishment of the pilot program, that periodically reviews single-family mortgage loans they own, guarantee, or securitize, using automated valuation models and other available data to assess current market value, and to identify borrowers who appear to satisfy equity and other requirements for cancellation of mortgage insurance.

(b)  The Director shall direct the Enterprises to establish procedures for the pilot program, including financial safety and soundness standards and payment-history requirements, under which mortgage insurance is canceled proactively when an Enterprise determines that:

(i)    the borrower satisfies applicable equity requirements based on the property’s current market value, as determined through an automated valuation model or other means approved by the Director;

(ii)   cancellation is consistent with financial safety and soundness and with the Enterprise’s contractual obligations; and

(iii)  the borrower satisfies all other applicable statutory, contractual, regulatory, and Enterprise requirements for cancellation.

(c)  The Director shall direct the Enterprises to require servicers, to the extent permitted by law and operationally feasible, to notify borrowers promptly when mortgage insurance may be canceled under the pilot program, and to reduce or eliminate unnecessary documentation requests, appraisal costs, and other administrative barriers to cancellation.

Sec. 3.  Standardizing the Permitting of Homes.  (a)  To increase the quality and lower the cost of building a home, there is hereby established the Task Force on Manufactured Housing Innovation (Task Force), which shall be co-chaired by the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development and the Director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency, or their designees, and shall include the Secretary of Agriculture, the Secretary of Commerce, and the Secretary of Veterans Affairs, or their designees.  The co-chairs may invite the heads of other executive departments and agencies (agencies) to participate, as appropriate.

(b)  Within 180 days of the date of this order, the Task Force shall submit to the President, through the Assistant to the President for Economic Policy, recommendations to facilitate the use of modern manufacturing methods in the production of manufactured and other factory-built housing eligible for Federal housing programs, including actions to:

(i)    promote specifications, certifications, inspections, and approvals across Federal housing and housing-finance programs;

(ii)   establish reciprocal recognition among agencies of licenses, certifications, approvals, and inspections, where doing so would avoid unnecessary duplication;

(iii)  eliminate Federal requirements and duplicative reviews that unnecessarily impede automation, modularization, standardized production, or other advanced manufacturing techniques, or that increase the time or cost of bringing homes to market;

(iv)   use Federal financing, insurance, guarantee, purchasing, and other program authorities to encourage innovation and increased production of affordable manufactured and factory-built homes; and

(v)    promote competition among manufacturers and other market participants while maintaining appropriate standards for safety, quality, durability, and consumer protection.

(c)  The Task Force shall also evaluate whether, and under what existing statutory authorities, Federal grant funding may be conditioned on, or be used to incentivize, State and local adoption of standardized permitting and licensing for manufactured and other factory-built housing, consistent with the best practices issued under section 4(a) of Executive Order 14394 of March 13, 2026 (Removing Regulatory Barriers to Affordable Home Construction), and shall prepare legislative recommendations to codify the policies set forth in this subsection.

(d)  The heads of the agencies represented on the Task Force shall, within their respective authorities, take appropriate action to implement the Task Force’s recommendations.

Sec. 4.  Reducing Excessive Title Insurance, Especially in the Refinancing of Americans Homes.  (a)  The Director shall, if he determines that it is in the best interests of the Enterprises or the FHFA, and the American public, and consistent with financial safety and soundness, the Director’s authorities as regulator and conservator, and applicable law, direct the Enterprises to expand the title acceptance pilot into an ongoing program, available nationwide through both Enterprises, under which an Enterprise may accept an automated title review or other title-risk assessment approved by the FHFA in lieu of a lender’s title insurance policy on eligible refinance transactions.

(b)  In expanding the program, the Director shall consider:

(i)    extending eligibility to refinance transactions with loan-to-value ratios above the current 80 percent limit where title risk remains low;

(ii)   removing geographic limitations and certifying additional title-assessment providers to promote competition;

(iii)  waiving appraisals, income re-verification, and other documentation requirements for limited cash-out refinances that reduce the borrower’s monthly payment, where the Enterprise’s existing data support doing so; and

(iv)   reducing or eliminating loan-level price adjustments and other Enterprise fees on such refinances.

(c)  The Director shall require that cost savings resulting from the program be passed through to borrowers and that lenders inform borrowers of those savings.

Sec. 5.  Department of Agriculture and Department of Veterans Affairs Direct Loan Rates.  The Secretary of Agriculture and the Secretary of Veterans Affairs shall, consistent with applicable law, including 42 U.S.C. 1490a(a)(1)(B) and 38 U.S.C. 3762(c)(1), and available appropriations, reduce the interest rates charged on single‑family home loans made directly by their respective departments.

Sec. 6.  General Provisions.  (a)  Nothing in this order shall be construed to impair or otherwise affect:

(i)   the authority granted by law to an executive department or agency, or the head thereof; or

(ii)  the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals.

(b)  This order shall be implemented consistent with applicable law and subject to the availability of appropriations.

(c)  This order is not intended to, and does not, create any right or benefit, substantive or procedural, enforceable at law or in equity by any party against the United States, its departments, agencies, or entities, its officers, employees, or agents, or any other person.

(d)  The costs for publication of this order shall be borne by the Federal Housing Finance Agency.

DONALD J. TRUMP

THE WHITE HOUSE,

         October 22, 2026.

MEMORANDUM FOR THE SECRETARY OF WAR

SUBJECT:       Presidential Determination Pursuant to Section 303 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as Amended, on Domestic Petroleum Production, Refining, and Logistics Capacity

On January 20, 2025, I issued Executive Order 14156 (Declaring a National Energy Emergency), under the National Emergencies Act.  That order found that America’s inadequate energy production, transportation, refining, and generation capacity constitute an unusual and extraordinary threat to the Nation’s economy, national security, and foreign policy.  It emphasized that our Nation’s current inadequate and intermittent energy supply leaves us vulnerable to hostile foreign actors and poses an imminent and growing threat to the prosperity and national security of the United States.

Consistent with that declaration, I find that ensuring resilient domestic petroleum production, refining, and logistics capacity is central to United States defense readiness.  Petroleum fuels the Nation’s Armed Forces, industrial base, and crucial infrastructure.  Without immediate Federal action, United States defense capabilities will remain vulnerable to disruption.

Therefore, by the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the laws of the United States of America, including section 303 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended (the “Act”) (50 U.S.C. 4533), I hereby determine, pursuant to section 303(a)(5) of the Act, that:

(1)  domestic petroleum production, refining, and logistics capacity, including exploration and production, gathering and transmission pipelines, storage, and marine terminals, are industrial resources, materials, or critical technology items essential to the national defense;

(2)  without Presidential action under section 303 of the Act, United States industry cannot reasonably be expected to provide these capabilities for the needed industrial resource, material, or critical technology item in a timely manner due to constrained financing, long lead times, permitting and infrastructure bottlenecks, and supply chain limitations; and

(3)  purchases, purchase commitments, financial support for the development of production capabilities, or other action pursuant to section 303 of the Act are the most cost-effective, expedient, and practical alternative methods for meeting this need.

I have declared a national emergency under Executive Order 14156, and I further determine that action to expand the domestic petroleum production, refining, and logistics capacity is necessary to avert an industrial resource or critical technology item shortfall that would severely impair national defense capability.  Therefore, pursuant to section 303(a)(7) of the Act, I waive the requirements of section 303(a)(1)-(a)(6) of the Act for the purpose of expanding such capability.

You are authorized and directed to implement this determination, including making necessary purchases, commitments, and financial instruments to enable these projects, and to publish this determination in the Federal Register.  Any provision of previous memoranda, proclamations, and Executive Orders that is inconsistent with this determination is superseded to the extent of such inconsistency.

                               DONALD J. TRUMP
